title: A HW/SW Co-Design of Video Dehazing Accelerator Using Decoupled Local Atmospheric Light Prior
problem: Video dehazing requires real-time processing to remove haze and atmospheric degradation from driving footage. Existing algorithms couple atmospheric light estimation with transmission estimation, limiting parallelization on hardware accelerators.
motivation: Haze and fog in autonomous driving scenarios impair perception and can cause accidents, necessitating real-time video dehazing with low power consumption.
method: The algorithm separates atmospheric light estimation (calculating haze intensity) from transmission estimation (determining how much light the haze blocks) into independent calculations. Since these two problems don't depend on each other, they can run at the same time on hardware accelerators (specialized chips like FPGAs or GPUs), making the whole process much faster than solving them one after the other. The approach is implemented on both FPGA and GPU, with software and hardware optimized separately to maximize parallel processing on each platform.
key_novelty: Decoupling atmospheric light and transmission calculation so they can both run simultaneously (at the same time) instead of one after the other, accelerating video dehazing on specialized hardware like FPGAs and GPUs.
contributions: Novel decoupled parallel architecture (DLAPID) for real-time video dehazing
Hardware-software co-design with deployment on both FPGA and GPU platforms
Demonstrated better dehazing performance with lower power consumption than SOTA methods
Validated on real-world driving scenarios and ground-truth datasets for autonomous vehicle safety
